name: Deneb
tagline: The tail of the Swan — one of the most distant naked-eye stars, blazing across 2,600 light-years.
history: Deneb is the most luminous star reliably visible to the naked eye — nearly 200,000 Suns compressed into a white supergiant so distant its light left around the Bronze Age. It crowns the Northern Cross and the Summer Triangle, and marks the Swan's tail in Cygnus. Precession will swing it near the north celestial pole around 9800 AD — a slow relay of pole stars that will make it Polaris's distant successor.
